title: Trump defends data centers in Ohio as he rallies to boost Jon Husted in a tight Senate race
source_used: Associated Press text read on Scripps News (AP original blocked, HTTP 403); The Hill for cross-check
key_facts: President Trump, at a campaign rally in Vandalia near Dayton, Ohio, on Saturday 3 Oct 2026, spent several minutes defending AI data centers: 'There's so much money to be made for Ohio. You can't just turn them off. They'll go to China.'
AP reports the crowd, enthusiastic on other topics, was far more muted during the data center remarks.

Trump said his administration is working to ensure data centers 'benefit local communities' and praised Sen. Jon Husted's bill asking utility regulators to charge large power users more; the Senate tried to advance it this week but nearly all Democrats blocked it.

Data centers are a central issue in the Ohio Senate race: Democrat Sherrod Brown attacks Husted, a former lieutenant governor, for giving 'billions in tax breaks to Big Tech' to bring data centers to Ohio.
AP describes data centers as a toxic political issue with bipartisan opposition over electricity prices, farmland and water.
The rally opens what Trump calls a 32-day blitz before the 3 Nov elections; Ohio is one of the Senate seats Democrats need to flip.
quote_evidence: "Look, there's so much money to be made for Ohio. You can't just turn them off. They'll go to China," Trump said, repeating his defense of data centers that he had made before.
The crowd, which had reacted enthusiastically as the president talked about other policies, was far more muted during the data centers remark.
"Senator Jon Husted gave billions in tax breaks to Big Tech to make sure they would build their data centers in Ohio," Brown wrote on X on Friday.
why_it_matters_hint: The president is campaigning for data centers in a swing state where his own voters fell quiet on the topic, a test of whether the AI buildout costs Republicans seats.
notes: AP original blocked (403); read the AP text as carried by Scripps News and cross-checked with The Hill's own report, which carries the same quotes. Follow-up of 1003:C05-01: new today is the Ohio rally, the muted crowd and the praise for Husted's blocked bill.
